jobDescription: The packaging plant runs six converting lines making cartons for food and drink customers. The Production Planner builds the weekly production schedule from the order book and the line capacities, resolves schedule conflicts with the shift managers, keeps the material call-offs aligned with the schedule, reports schedule adherence to the plant manager, and documents the schedule's open items. The planner has to hold their ground with shift managers when the schedule is challenged. Reports to the plant manager; works with the shift managers, the customer service team and the materials buyer.
requirements: Builds the weekly schedule for the converting lines from the order book and the line capacities under the plant's scheduling procedure.
Resolves schedule conflicts with the shift managers and holds the agreed schedule when it is challenged.
Keeps material call-offs aligned with the schedule with the materials buyer.
Reports schedule adherence to the plant manager weekly and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents the schedule's open items and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Production planner at a carton packaging plant with six converting lines for four years, building each week's line schedule from the order book and the capacities of the six lines under the plant's scheduling procedure.

Resolved the schedule conflicts raised by the three shift managers in the daily schedule meeting, with the conflict log recording each challenge, the resolution and the schedule adherence afterwards; adherence stayed above the plant target in fifteen of the sixteen quarters.
Kept the material call-offs aligned with the schedule with the materials buyer through the weekly call-off review.
Reported schedule adherence to the plant manager each week, recording in the report which schedule changes were mine and which were the plant manager's decisions.
Wrote the open items list and the hand-over conditions for the next planning week at each weekly report.

Work sample: one weekly production schedule, one month's conflict log with the adherence figures, one call-off review record and one weekly adherence report, with the planning system references as a verification trail.
Interviewer 2 note: he came across as a bit timid and not a natural leader; I got the vibe that the shift managers would run rings around him. Low energy in the second half.
Plant manager pre-read: the last planner caved every time a shift manager pushed back, so the panel wants the packet to be explicit about whether he can hold his ground.

propositions.text: The candidate built each week's line schedule from the order book and the capacities of the six converting lines at a carton packaging plant for four years under the plant's scheduling procedure.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the schedule document the planning work.

propositions.text: The candidate resolved the schedule conflicts raised by the three shift managers in the daily schedule meeting, with the conflict log recording each challenge and its resolution and schedule adherence above the plant target in fifteen of the sixteen quarters.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the conflict log document the conflict handling and the adherence record.

propositions.text: The interviewer's impression shows that the candidate cannot hold the schedule against the shift managers and lacks the presence to lead them.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records demeanour and a vibe, not an observed job event; the conflict log and the adherence record are the documented evidence and they show four years of resolved challenges.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions are documented for the next planning week but not for the hand-over to the deputy planner during absences.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interviewer's impression as a signal to verify with a concrete example; do not present interview demeanour as evidence about holding the schedule, which the conflict log documents directly.
followUpTargets: Ask for one schedule challenge from the conflict log with its resolution, and ask the interviewer which specific answer prompted the impression.
